findings.title: Migration fails when no embed category is configured
findings.body: The category query unconditionally indexes row 0 before converting the ID to an integer. If embed_category is unset (its default is empty), or names a category that no longer exists, the query returns no rows and this access raises instead of reaching the uncategorized fallback. Consequently, ordinary installations without embedding configured cannot run this migration or upgrade. Check for an empty result before reading the ID, and handle an absent fallback setting as well.

findings.title: Normalize existing allowed hosts during migration
findings.body: The migration inserts old embeddable_hosts entries verbatim, bypassing the new model's normalization callback. The old host check supported entries such as http://eviltrout.com and https://eviltrout.com, but the new lookup compares the stored value directly against URI.host, such as eviltrout.com. Those migrated entries will never match, so previously working embeds and topic retrieval stop working after upgrade. Normalize the migrated entries before inserting them.

findings.title: Hosts saved with ports can never match an embedding URL
findings.body: The host validator accepts entries such as example.com:8080, and the normalization callback preserves the port. record_for_host, however, extracts only URI.host and compares example.com against the stored example.com:8080. Thus an administrator can successfully save a port-qualified host but all requests from it are rejected and its category mapping is never used. Normalize storage and lookup consistently, or reject port-qualified entries explicitly.

findings.title: Host validation rejects valid long top-level domains
findings.body: The new validation restricts the final domain label to two through five letters. Valid embedding hosts such as example.museum or example.technology therefore cannot be added or saved, despite being ordinary DNS hostnames supported by the previous host lookup. Use hostname validation that supports valid longer top-level domains rather than this five-character limit.
